newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse drops for third consecutive week.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse drops for third consecutive week.

text.p: The Casablanca bourse closed on Friday lower 0.11 percent, pursuing its decline for the third consecutive week, stockbrokers said.
The drop was due to the market volatility and profit-taking by foreign investors, they said.
The all-share index closed at 433.24 points, down from 434.37 points last Friday.
Wafabank, a liquid stock, lost four dirhams in a week to close at 536 dirhams.
"The bourse index movement was in fact a consolidation of market stocks except for the Samir refinery," Hassan Bouhamou, head of a Casablanca-based funds management firm said.
Samir, Morocco's main oil refinery, lost four dirhams to close at 246 dirhams.
"Samir shares drop is unjustified...I think there is lack of communication on the market," he said.
Despite the recent decline, "the bourse index will remain steady and over the threshold of 400 points by end 1996 due to an excellent valorisation ratio," Bouhamou added.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest private conglomerate closed at 550, lost eight dirhams to 550 dirhams
SNI has diversified stakes in more than 40 companies.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of the market's largest capitalisation, remained stagnant at 395 dirhams compared with the previous week.
Traded volume on the official market was 20.6 million dirhams, down from 38.8 million dirhams last Friday.
